project.title: Cannae: The Centre Bends
project.location: Cannae, Apulia, beside the River Aufidus
project.production_mode: original illustrated 2D proof of motion; picture-only; no audio cue is approved
historical_basis: Polybius, Histories Book III, account of the battle of Cannae
Oxford Classical Dictionary, Cannae battle summary
project.interpretive_caveat: The five shots are a schematic explanation of the enveloping manoeuvre, not a surveyed reconstruction of exact unit positions, head counts or minute-by-minute movement. Ancient casualty figures and force strengths are deliberately omitted.
project.sound_status: silent_picture_proof; all music and Foley deferred until exact samples are human-auditioned

shots.story_purpose: Locate Cannae beside the Aufidus and make the river plain legible before showing the armies.
shots.location: Apulia map and the river Aufidus
shots.time_of_day: historical map graphic; no literal time of day
shots.visual_state_change: Parchment contours emerge; the river draws across the plain; Cannae is marked; two army tokens enter the field.

camera.motivation: Push toward the river bend to move from regional context to the battlefield location.
camera.end: close view of the Aufidus bend

environment_layers.motion: contour lines reveal in staggered bands

shots.story_purpose: Show the Roman infantry mass advancing and establish why the centre becomes the point of pressure.
shots.visual_state_change: Front-rank soldiers step forward in staggered rhythm; rear ranks emerge through dust; standards and cloak hems move in the crosswind.

camera.motivation: Track beside the front rank to reveal the depth and forward momentum of the Roman formation.

characters.blocking: marches toward the opposing line with shield close to the body
characters.acting_notes: feet alternate with visible ground contact; shield stays attached to the forearm

characters.blocking: moves in offset rows behind the front rank
characters.acting_notes: cycle phase offsets prevent synchronized repetition

props.reaction: small weight response with each step

environment_layers.motion: occasional dust sweeps across the lower frame
branches and leaves move in wind

shots.story_purpose: Make the crucial centre movement readable: Hannibal's forward-curving centre yields under pressure instead of holding a rigid line.
shots.visual_state_change: The central line begins convex; Roman pressure advances; the centre bends backward; shields and bodies react while dust rolls through the contact zone.

camera.motivation: Push toward the bending line so the audience reads the centre giving ground, not a generic weapon montage.
camera.start: two front-rank figures in medium close
camera.end: tight view of the bowing central line

characters.blocking: steps back in a controlled arc while maintaining facing
characters.acting_notes: weight shifts backward; avoid depicting a chaotic rout

characters.role: Roman infantry at the point of pressure
characters.blocking: leans and steps forward into the narrowing centre
characters.acting_notes: shield and torso move as one; shoulders compress on contact

props.reaction: the defender's shield and shoulder recoil, then settle

environment_layers.motion: dust blooms outward at contact then falls
successive rank silhouettes follow the centre's backward curve

shots.story_purpose: Explain how the wings and cavalry movement threaten the exposed sides and rear as the Roman mass presses inward.
shots.location: overhead battlefield diagram transitioning into a high oblique view
shots.visual_state_change: Two flank markers pivot inward; cavalry paths sweep around the outer edges; the Roman mass remains compressed in the middle.

camera.motivation: Reframe from the bowed centre to both flanks so the audience understands the enclosing geometry.

characters.blocking: moves around the exposed side toward the rear
characters.gaze: toward the rear of the Roman formation
characters.acting_notes: horse and rider remain mechanically linked; use staggered gait phases

characters.role: Carthaginian cavalry from the opposing wing
characters.blocking: joins the enclosing movement behind the infantry mass
characters.acting_notes: use a distinct path and timing from the other cavalry group

environment_layers.motion: dust follows the left cavalry arc
dust follows the right cavalry arc
terrain remains stable during the tactical reveal

shots.story_purpose: Resolve the tactical explanation: the Roman mass is increasingly surrounded as the flanks converge behind it.
shots.visual_state_change: The two outer arcs meet behind the Roman mass; escape paths diminish; the frame settles on the enclosing shape and the place/date.

camera.motivation: Pull back to reveal the full enclosing geometry rather than treating the contact as an isolated duel.
camera.start: high oblique on the rear of the Roman line

characters.blocking: holds compressed in the centre with limited room to turn
characters.acting_notes: movement becomes constrained, not a synchronized collapse

characters.blocking: turn inward to narrow the surrounding arc
characters.gaze: toward the interior of the encirclement

environment_layers.motion: fine dust drifts across the lower edge
haze softens the far ridge while keeping silhouettes readable

graphics.text: THE CENTRE BENDS. THE FLANKS CLOSE.
